Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

outline verb

sketch out the main points of a story or essay

also outline the story, outline the essay, summarise briefly, sketch out, classroom commands, trace (outline)

classical

Varr. RR 2 pr. 7: breviter ac summātim percurram (Lewis & Short s.v. summātim)
Cic. Att. 5.16.1: aliquid summātim perscrībere (Lewis & Short)

summātim percurrere

adverb with percurrō; also summātim perscrībere, write out in brief

run briefly over the main points

Other words

  • dēlīneō, dēlīneāre, dēlīneāvī, dēlīneātum — sketch out (a drawing)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plin. NH 35.89: imāginem in pariete carbōne (Lewis & Short); Traupman 34: outline the story, dēlīneā (dēlīneāte) fābulam (tractātum); Traupman 397 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    In Lewis & Short only of sketching a picture; we have found no classical instance of it for outlining a story or an essay, as Traupman uses it.

  • dēlīneātiō, dēlīneātiōnis f. — an outline, a sketch

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Traupman 355 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: late Latin (Tertullian) for fōrma, dēscrīptiō.

Examples

  • Dēlīneā (dēlīneāte) fābulam (tractātum).

    Outline the story (the essay).Traupman 34

See also in short, draw.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
